inertiaPresets.label: 1 wheel
inertiaPresets.detail: One 96 mm Gecko + hub + shaft: 1.21e-4 + 0.05e-4 ≈ 1.3e-4 kg·m²

inertiaPresets.label: 2 wheels + steel flywheel
inertiaPresets.detail: Two 96 mm Geckos + one 82 mm goBILDA Steel Flywheel + hubs: 2 × 1.21e-4 + 1.65e-4 + 0.1e-4 ≈ 4.2e-4, rounded to 4.0e-4 kg·m² (the SPEC §9 reference inertia; within the ±25 % wheel estimate)

inertiaPresets.label: 2 wheels + 3 steel flywheels
inertiaPresets.detail: Two 96 mm Geckos + three 82 mm goBILDA Steel Flywheels + hubs: 2 × 1.21e-4 + 3 × 1.65e-4 + 0.1e-4 ≈ 7.5e-4 kg·m²

notes: Wheel inertia: I = k·m·r² with r = D/2 and m from goBILDA's spec table. Gecko wheels (silicone spokes and tread on a small plastic core) use the solid-disc value k = 0.5, which is slightly conservative. Hogback and Rhino wheels (rigid plastic core with a rubber tread band at the rim) use a rim-weighted k = 0.6. For comparison, goBILDA's published steel flywheel values work out to k = 0.53 (60 mm) and k = 0.65 (82 mm). Treat the wheel values as ±25 %.

Inertia on one shaft adds up: wheels + hubs + steel discs. An inertia wheel geared to spin g times faster than the shooter wheel counts as g²·I. Hubs and the 8 mm REX shaft add about 5e-6 kg·m² each. goBILDA does not publish motor rotor inertia, so it is left out; it is small next to these presets.

Inertia presets are per wheel shaft. Two 96 mm wheels plus hubs alone come to only about 2.5e-4 kg·m². Reaching the ≈4e-4 default takes one 82 mm steel flywheel, so the medium label says that. goBILDA lists this flywheel as a related product for its DECODE Starter Bot, and its product page describes it as a way to add rotational inertia to launcher systems.
15A-durometer GripForce Gecko variants weigh about the same (96 mm 15A: 102 g), so they can reuse the 30A entries.

etaSingle 0.45 (kept). In no-slip theory the ball rolls on the fixed hood, so its centre leaves at 0.5 × the wheel's surface speed at the moment of exit (Brettle 2023; Team 449, 2026). The wheel also slows during the shot. Measured against the pre-shot set speed, the ideal ratio for POLLEN is 0.47 at I = 4e-4 and 0.42 at I = 1.3e-4. FRC teams shooting squishy foam balls report lower values: 30 % was standard in one team's prototypes, and 20–45 % is a typical guess (Chief Delphi, 2021). A tennis-ball test posted in 2026 reached about 56 % of the ideal kinetic energy, which is about 0.37 of surface speed. So 0.45 is the optimistic end. It fits a stiff hollow ball on a soft 30A wheel with light compression. Calibrate it with slow-motion video. At 0.35, every required wheel rpm goes up by 29 %.

etaDual 0.90 (kept). In the ideal model, a ball squeezed between two counter-rotating wheels leaves at the average of their two surface speeds (Team 449 dual-flywheel model, as used in ReCalc; Chief Delphi, 2021). Counting the wheels slowing during contact, the ideal is about 0.91 at a combined 4e-4 kg·m² and 0.95 at 7.5e-4. Slip and compression losses pull real shooters lower; 0.75–0.90 is plausible.

lossFactor 2.0 (kept). In the no-slip impulse model the wheel loses twice the ball's translational + rotational kinetic energy in the high-inertia limit, for both the single-wheel hood and the dual-wheel case, so efficiency is at most 50 % (Brettle 2023). The value computed for POLLEN at I = 4e-4 is 2.06. Real slip only adds loss, so 2.0 is a floor; 2–3.5 is plausible.

Spin: single hood S0 = 1 (the ball rolls on the hood, so ω·r = v). Dual S0 = (1 − k)/(1 + k), which matches the Team 449 relations v = (v1 + v2)/2 and ω·r = (v1 − v2)/2. The default topRatio 0.6 gives S0 = 0.25.

Headroom (sigmaMotor knees 0.80 / 0.95 and downgradeHeadroom 0.92, kept) matches common practice. Size the shooter so the shot speed is reachable at about 8 V of a 12 V battery (Chief Delphi, 2016). Set the target at the speed the wheel reaches with about 10 V applied, roughly 0.74–0.80 of full-battery free speed (FTC DECODE shooter blog, 2025). Leave 10–30 % headroom above the on-shot speed (YETI wiki).

DECODE (2025-26) sanity check. Fixed ~58–60° DECODE shooters needed about 4.4–6.9 m/s to score the 5 in, 0.165 lb perforated ARTIFACT balls. At etaSingle 0.45 on a 96 mm wheel, that is about 1,930–3,050 wheel rpm, or 32–51 % of a 6000 rpm motor at G = 1. goBILDA's DECODE Starter Bot sample code holds its single high-speed launcher motor (driving two launcher wheels) at 1,125 encoder counts/s for close shots. If that motor is the 28-count 6000 rpm Yellow Jacket, that is about 2,410 rpm, or 40 % of free speed. The BIOBUZZ POLLEN reference shot (5.05 m/s → about 2,230 wheel rpm, h ≈ 0.37 on a 96 mm hood) sits in the same range.
SPEC §9 motor check with these values: 6000 rpm motor, 96 mm wheel, single hood, 5.05 m/s exit → 2,233 wheel rpm, h = 0.372. With I = 4.0e-4 (medium preset), POLLEN dip = 4.87 %.
No external data backs sigmaMotor, the verdict thresholds or the precision presets. They are SPEC design choices and are carried over unchanged.
freeSpeedFactor 0.97: goBILDA lists the bare 1:1 motor at 6000 rpm theoretical and 5800 rpm tested; usable free speed = freeRpm x 0.97.
